capabilities: Render DBML models as ER diagrams from code blocks in notes
Read .dbml files from disk, including paths outside the vault
Filter which tables a diagram shows by name
Set each block's height and light or dark theme
Re-read on-screen models with a Refresh diagrams command
disambiguation: Not a DBML editor; it only renders existing .dbml files as diagrams and never writes them.
extras: Desktop only (reads files with Node's fs). The bundled diagram frame is about 16.4 MB of HTML and each loaded diagram costs roughly 70 MB of memory. Reader-facing text is English or Russian depending on Obsidian's language. Sends nothing over the network.
motivation: The models a documentation vault draws usually live beside the documentation they describe (an Antora or MkDocs site's models/), and copying them into the vault would leave two versions to drift apart.
problem: Obsidian cannot draw DBML database models, and diagram tools that embed a web renderer usually need the model copied into the vault or fetched over the network.

relations.evidence: frame/embed.html is DBML Studio's frame (the dbml-frame package)
The keys are the MkDocs plugin's (DBML Studio's packages/mkdocs-dbml)

summary: Renders DBML database models as ER diagrams in note code blocks, reading .dbml files from disk, including files outside the vault.
